title: engineering-all-hands-2026-04-29
content:
Engineering All-Hands Notes — 2026-04-29

Attendees: All engineering org (recording in #eng-all-hands).
Hosts: Alex Chen (platform eng), Priya Nair (serving runtime lead).
Duration: 45 min

TL;DR:
- Production rollout of autoscaler v2 completed for the eu-west-1 Dedicated pool; avg tail latency improved 18% under burst load.
- Incident postmortem published for the 2026-04-21 KV-cache outage (see link below). Primary action items: additional cache eviction telemetry + canary for cache config changes.
- Next sprint focus: Private deployment KMS integration (phase 1), Dedicated burst policy refactor, and Reduce-cost pilot for embedding pipelines.
- Hiring: two infra SDEs and one SRE offer extended; recruiting ramping for Platform Observability PM.

Agenda / Notes:
1) Metrics & recent changes
   - Autoscaler v2 rollout status (Priya)
     - Deployed to eu-west-1 Dedicated cluster on 2026-04-25 during low-traffic window. Canary ran for 48h.
     - Results: 18% improvement in p95 inference latency under 10% burst traffic; 7% reduction in instance-hours for steady-state workloads.
     - Rollout to us-east-1 planned next week (2026-05-06). See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Autoscaler-Design-Doc
   - Cost & capacity update (Diego)
     - Dedicated utilization: avg 62% across reserved pools; autoscaler reduces overprovision by ~12% on test workloads.
     - Action: platform-cost working group to propose instance sizing changes by 2026-05-10.

2) Incident recap: KV-cache outage (2026-04-21) — summary (Alex)
   - What happened: a cache-config change during a routine deploy caused aggressive expiration to be enabled in one AZ; that triggered mass miss storms and higher load on model-serving pods, causing throttling and elevated latency for ~37 minutes.
   - Impact: increased p99 latencies for hosted API and delayed responses for Dedicated customers in the affected region. No data lost.
   - Root cause: insufficient canarying of cache-config flags + missing guardrail in the control-plane API.
   - Remediations completed: reverted config, added temporary traffic-shift rule.
   - Permanent fixes in progress: (a) add preflight canary in control-plane for cache flags (ENG-2389), (b) telemetry to detect cache miss storms, (c) automated rollback on hit-threshold.
   - Postmortem link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/KV-Cache-Outage-2026-04-21

3) Roadmap highlights & quarterly goals
   - Private deployments: KMS integration (phase 1) — timeline Q2 end. Goal: support BYOK flow for customer-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS connectors. Owners: Samir + Security.
   - Observability: token-level cost trace links in console (MVP shipping mid-May). This will let customers see per-request cost with model route breakdowns.
   - Serving runtime: planning performance sweep for LLM attention kernels for long-context models (owner: Priya).

4) Engineering process / org updates
   - Oncall rotation change: two-person oncall for weekend windows starting 2026-05-01. New schedule posted in Confluence and PagerDuty.
   - RFC process reminder: any infra-facing config changes that touch autoscaler or cache must include a small canary plan and rollback steps in the RFC.

5) Demos & highlights
   - Demo: autoscaler v2 canary dashboard walkthrough (Diego). Dashboard shows rapid scale-up and safe scale-down behavior; new alert on abnormal scale-activity correlated with error rates.
   - Quick show: new per-route latency histogram in console (screenshot in Confluence).

6) People & hiring
   - Headcount: hiring for 2 infra SDEs and 1 SRE (offers extended). Expect joiners in June.
   - Kudos: Platform Observability team for landing the new trace UI; Runtime team for the kernel opt prototype.

7) Blockers & asks
   - Private/KMS: Security needs a short design review with Platform and Solutions Eng to finalize HSM key rotation cadence. Owner: Samir. Target: 2026-05-03.
   - Load-testing: need more realistic workload traces from Hosting product for embeddings pipelines. Action: Hosting PM to share sample dataset (deadline 2026-05-05).
   - Storage gating: release of cold-cache tier blocked on egress-cost estimate from Cloud FinOps. Finance to provide numbers by 2026-05-07.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Autoscaler runbook update with rollback playbook — Priya — due 2026-05-04.
- Cache-miss telemetry prototype & canary plan — Alex + Runtime — due 2026-05-06.
- Observability cost-trace beta invites — Diego — due 2026-05-10.
- KMS design review meeting — Samir + Security — schedule by 2026-05-03.

Q&A highlights:
- Q: Any plan to open-source parts of the autoscaler?
  A: There's interest in extracting generic components, but no public timeline. We'll evaluate licensing implications and internal cleanup first.
- Q: Will Dedicated customers see any config changes requiring action?
  A: No immediate changes; any config toggles will be rolled out with canaries and announced via the customer changelog.

Notes / links referenced in the meeting:
- Autoscaler design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Autoscaler-Design-Doc
- KV-cache postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/KV-Cache-Outage-2026-04-21
- RFC: ENG-2389
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1428

Appendix: quick status table (one-line summaries)
- Autoscaler v2: rolled out canary -> eu-west-1 completed; us-east-1 next.
- KV-cache fixes: telemetry + canary plan in progress.
- Private/KMS: design phase, sec review scheduled.
- Observability: cost tracing beta mid-May.

If you weren't able to attend, recording and slides are in #eng-all-hands and the Confluence page above. Please add questions to the thread or ping the owners directly.

— Alex (platform eng)
